NEWS FROM THE BOARD NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. September 2024 Tom Dayley - Commissioner Rod Beck - Board Chairman Ryan Davidson - Commissioner By the time you read this article the November 5th General Election will be just days away. If you have any questions about where to vote, when to vote, absentee ballots, voting early or if you’re curious to see what your ballot will look like, there’s an easy one-stop place to get answers for any questions you may have. Ada County Elections does an outstanding job of making sure election information is readily available to anyone who needs it. Visit the Ada County website and learn more. https://adacounty.id.gov/elections/

# Page 2^page=2
Domestic Violence can have far reaching and long-lasting effects on not just the victim, but their children, in-laws, neighbors, even co-workers. Imagine putting in a long day at work and then heading home to a place where things aren’t really that safe. The anxiety that creates can wreak havoc on someone’s life. Your co-workers may notice it, your friends sense something is wrong. It’s so important to know that there are resources where a person can reach out for help. No judgement. No shame. October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month. A way to shine the light on something that can cause immeasurable harm. The Ada County Commissioners are deeply appreciative that each year Bea Black and her team at the Women’s and Children’s Alliance (WCA) invite officials from around the Treasure Valley to gather in Meridian at the Idaho Peace OCTOBER IS DOMESTIC VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH Officers Memorial. Each year these officials sign a proclamation recognizing the importance of Domestic Violence Awareness. Elected officials and law enforcement from both Ada and Canyon County were on hand for the event. Thank you to everyone who attended including Ada County Sheriff’s Office, Ada County Prosecutor’s Office, Ada County Victim Services Center and so many others. Pictured Left-Right Ada County Commission Chairman Rod Beck, Ada County Commissioner Tom Dayley, Ada County Prosecutor Jan Bennetts, Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford, Ada County Victim Services Center Director Trina Allen, Victim Services Coordinator Aileen Arredondo, Ada County Domestic Violence Court Program Coordinator Jeniffer Rae and Ada County EMS Director Shawn Rayne 2

# Page 3^page=3
UNPLUG AND PLAY Toys for Tots toy distribution event at Barber Park draws thousands Ada County Commissioners Rod Beck (Chairman) and Tom Dayley along with Ada County Sheriff Matt Clifford attended the Toys for Tots ‘Unplug and Play’ toy distribution event at Ada County’s Barber Park September 15th. We were honored to have members of the United States Marine Corps on hand as honored guests. The event is part an effort to encourage children to spend more time away from their screens and to enjoy the outdoors - interacting with nature and one another. 3000 people over five hours stopped by! The Barber Park toy giveaway featured bouncy houses, and great food. A whopping 14,000 toys were handed out to kids and families. In August 30,000 toys were handed out during the last day of the Western Idaho Fair. If you’d like to learn more about the Toys for Tots ‘Unplug and Play’ program – how you can donate and participate - please contact local charity https:// www.astegos.org/ 3

4 TOBIN BOLTER MEMORIAL KIDS DUATHLON The community couldn’t have asked for better weather for the Tobin Bolter Memorial Kids Duathlon September 20th. This was the 8th annual Kids Duathlon and from here on out it will be officially named the Tobin Bolter Memorial Kids Duathlon to honor fallen Ada County Sheriff’s Office deputy Tobin Bolter. Thank you to Ada County Development Services for planning and coordinating such a wonderful event. Thank you to all the little athletes and their parents for participating. We are a healthy, outdoors-loving community and this event allows us to give something back to everyone who calls Ada County home! 4

5 ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes thirteen individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks and waterways, public defense, indigent services, juvenile court, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more. Learn more about the services provided to you by Ada County www.adacounty.id.gov/ 5

# Page 6^page=6
ASSESSORS AWARD 2024 We’re pleased to announce that the Ada County Assessor’s Office completed recertification of the Certificate of Excellence in Assessment Administration (CEAA). This certification is granted by the International Associated of Assessing Officers (IAAO) and follows a rigorous review of internal processes to confirm compliance with industry best-practices. There are over 13,000 assessment jurisdictions in the US and only 59 have achieved this recognition. The Ada County Assessor’s Office was first awarded this certificate in 2012 – at the time only the 17th jurisdiction in the world to qualify and the 2nd in the Western US – and have successfully met recertification requirements twice since then. The 2024 recertification affirms our continued commitment to meeting IAAO’s standards and, more importantly, shows us where we have room to improve and grow. The IAAO grading team summarized the submission by stating “The detailed narrative demonstrates Ada County’s continuous strive for excellence in managing work related to assessment and tax, as well as in serving the public.” Learn More about Career Opportunities and Ada County’s Benefits Package https://adacounty.id.gov/human-resources/ 6
